message.content:
In this repository, there is a markdown processing interface (some interface/protocol/abstract type for rendering or parsing Markdown). I need to find:
1. The interface/type definition itself (file path, line, name)
2. All concrete implementation(s) of that interface that execute at runtime
3. Who constructs/instantiates those implementations (constructor call sites, DI registration, factory functions)
4. Which components/structs/classes hold a reference to the interface (i.e., depend on it via the interface type, not the concrete type)

Search broadly: try terms like "Markdown", "markdown", "MarkdownRenderer", "MarkdownProcessor", "MarkdownService", "Renderer" interface, goldmark, blackfriday, markdown-it, commonmark, remark, marked. Check across the whole repo (could be Go, TypeScript, Python, etc - inspect the repo structure first).

Report back with exact file paths and line numbers for: the interface definition, each concrete implementation, each construction/instantiation site, and each holder (field/struct that types against the interface).

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	package renderer
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"bytes"
     5		"fmt"
     6		"strings"
     7	
     8		gast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
     9		east "github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension/ast"
    10	
    11		mast "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/markdown/ast"
    12	)
    13	
    14	// MarkdownRenderer renders goldmark AST back to markdown text.
    15	type MarkdownRenderer struct {
    16		buf *bytes.Buffer
    17	}
    18	
    19	// NewMarkdownRenderer creates a new markdown renderer.
    20	func NewMarkdownRenderer() *MarkdownRenderer {
    21		return &MarkdownRenderer{
    22			buf: &bytes.Buffer{},
    23		}
    24	}
    25	
    26	// Render renders the AST node to markdown and returns the result.
    27	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) Render(node gast.Node, source []byte) string {
    28		r.buf.Reset()
    29		r.renderNode(node, source, 0)
    30		return r.buf.String()
    31	}
    32	
    33	// renderNode renders a single node and its children.
    34	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderNode(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
    35		switch n := node.(type) {
    36		case *gast.Document:
    37			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    38	
    39		case *gast.Paragraph:
    40			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    41			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
    42				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
    43			}
    44	
    45		case *gast.Text:
    46			// Text nodes store their content as segments in the source
    47			segment := n.Segment
    48			r.buf.Write(segment.Value(source))
    49			if n.SoftLineBreak() {
    50				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
    51			} else if n.HardLineBreak() {
    52				r.buf.WriteString("  \n")
    53			}
    54	
    55		case *gast.CodeSpan:
    56			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
    57			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    58			r.buf.WriteByte('`')
    59	
    60		case *gast.Emphasis:
    61			symbol := "*"
    62			if n.Level == 2 {
    63				symbol = "**"
    64			}
    65			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
    66			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    67			r.buf.WriteString(symbol)
    68	
    69		case *gast.Link:
    70			r.buf.WriteString("[")
    71			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    72			r.buf.WriteString("](")
    73			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
    74			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
    75				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
    76				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
    77				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
    78			}
    79			r.buf.WriteString(")")
    80	
    81		case *gast.AutoLink:
    82			url := n.URL(source)
    83			if n.AutoLinkType == gast.AutoLinkEmail {
    84				r.buf.WriteString("<")
    85				r.buf.Write(url)
    86				r.buf.WriteString(">")
    87			} else {
    88				r.buf.Write(url)
    89			}
    90	
    91		case *gast.Image:
    92			r.buf.WriteString("![")
    93			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
    94			r.buf.WriteString("](")
    95			r.buf.Write(n.Destination)
    96			if len(n.Title) > 0 {
    97				r.buf.WriteString(` "`)
    98				r.buf.Write(n.Title)
    99				r.buf.WriteString(`"`)
   100			}
   101			r.buf.WriteString(")")
   102	
   103		case *gast.Heading:
   104			r.buf.WriteString(strings.Repeat("#", n.Level))
   105			r.buf.WriteByte(' ')
   106			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
   107			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   108				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   109			}
   110	
   111		case *gast.CodeBlock, *gast.FencedCodeBlock:
   112			r.renderCodeBlock(n, source)
   113	
   114		case *gast.Blockquote:
   115			// Render each child line with "> " prefix
   116			r.renderBlockquote(n, source, depth)
   117			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   118				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   119			}
   120	
   121		case *gast.List:
   122			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
   123			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   124				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   125			}
   126	
   127		case *gast.ListItem:
   128			r.renderListItem(n, source, depth)
   129	
   130		case *gast.ThematicBreak:
   131			r.buf.WriteString("---")
   132			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   133				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   134			}
   135	
   136		case *east.Strikethrough:
   137			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
   138			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
   139			r.buf.WriteString("~~")
   140	
   141		case *east.TaskCheckBox:
   142			if n.IsChecked {
   143				r.buf.WriteString("[x] ")
   144			} else {
   145				r.buf.WriteString("[ ] ")
   146			}
   147	
   148		case *east.Table:
   149			r.renderTable(n, source)
   150			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   151				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   152			}
   153	
   154		// Custom Memos nodes
   155		case *mast.TagNode:
   156			r.buf.WriteByte('#')
   157			r.buf.Write(n.Tag)
   158	
   159		case *mast.MentionNode:
   160			r.buf.WriteByte('@')
   161			r.buf.Write(n.Username)
   162	
   163		default:
   164			// For unknown nodes, try to render children
   165			r.renderChildren(n, source, depth)
   166		}
   167	}
   168	
   169	// renderChildren renders all children of a node.
   170	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderChildren(node gast.Node, source []byte, depth int) {
   171		child := node.FirstChild()
   172		for child != nil {
   173			r.renderNode(child, source, depth+1)
   174			child = child.NextSibling()
   175		}
   176	}
   177	
   178	// renderCodeBlock renders a code block.
   179	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderCodeBlock(node gast.Node, source []byte) {
   180		if fenced, ok := node.(*gast.FencedCodeBlock); ok {
   181			// Fenced code block with language
   182			r.buf.WriteString("```")
   183			if lang := fenced.Language(source); len(lang) > 0 {
   184				r.buf.Write(lang)
   185			}
   186			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
   187	
   188			// Write all lines
   189			lines := fenced.Lines()
   190			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
   191				line := lines.At(i)
   192				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
   193			}
   194	
   195			r.buf.WriteString("```")
   196			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   197				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   198			}
   199		} else if codeBlock, ok := node.(*gast.CodeBlock); ok {
   200			// Indented code block
   201			lines := codeBlock.Lines()
   202			for i := 0; i < lines.Len(); i++ {
   203				line := lines.At(i)
   204				r.buf.WriteString("    ")
   205				r.buf.Write(line.Value(source))
   206			}
   207			if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   208				r.buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   209			}
   210		}
   211	}
   212	
   213	// renderBlockquote renders a blockquote with "> " prefix.
   214	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderBlockquote(node *gast.Blockquote, source []byte, depth int) {
   215		// Create a temporary buffer for the blockquote content
   216		tempBuf := &bytes.Buffer{}
   217		tempRenderer := &MarkdownRenderer{buf: tempBuf}
   218		tempRenderer.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
   219	
   220		// Add "> " prefix to each line
   221		content := tempBuf.String()
   222		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(content, "\n"), "\n")
   223		for i, line := range lines {
   224			r.buf.WriteString("> ")
   225			r.buf.WriteString(line)
   226			if i < len(lines)-1 {
   227				r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
   228			}
   229		}
   230	}
   231	
   232	// renderListItem renders a list item with proper indentation and markers.
   233	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderListItem(node *gast.ListItem, source []byte, depth int) {
   234		parent := node.Parent()
   235		list, ok := parent.(*gast.List)
   236		if !ok {
   237			r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
   238			return
   239		}
   240	
   241		// Add indentation only for nested lists
   242		// Document=0, List=1, ListItem=2 (no indent), nested ListItem=3+ (indent)
   243		if depth > 2 {
   244			indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth-2)
   245			r.buf.WriteString(indent)
   246		}
   247	
   248		// Add list marker
   249		if list.IsOrdered() {
   250			fmt.Fprintf(r.buf, "%d. ", list.Start)
   251			list.Start++ // Increment for next item
   252		} else {
   253			r.buf.WriteString("- ")
   254		}
   255	
   256		// Render content
   257		r.renderChildren(node, source, depth)
   258	
   259		// Add newline if there's a next sibling
   260		if node.NextSibling() != nil {
   261			r.buf.WriteByte('\n')
   262		}
   263	}
   264	
   265	// renderTable renders a table in markdown format.
   266	func (r *MarkdownRenderer) renderTable(table *east.Table, source []byte) {
   267		// This is a simplified table renderer
   268		// A full implementation would need to handle alignment, etc.
   269		r.renderChildren(table, source, 0)
   270	}

## Findings

This is a Go backend (`github.com/usememos/memos`). The markdown processing interface is `markdown.Service`. I checked the frontend (`web/src/`) too — it only has plain data-shape TS `interface`s for AST node types (e.g. `web/src/types/markdown.ts`, `web/src/components/MemoContent/markdown/types.ts`) used with `react-markdown`; there is no swappable renderer interface there. The real interface/implementation/DI story lives in Go.

### 1. Interface definition
- **File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
- **Line 31:** `type Service interface { ... }`
  - Methods: `ExtractAll`, `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenderMarkdown`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet`, `ValidateContent`, `RenameTag` (lines 33–54).

### 2. Concrete implementation
- **File:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
- **Line 58:** `type service struct { md goldmark.Markdown }` — the sole runtime implementation of `Service`.
  - Methods implementing the interface (same file): `parse` (116), `ExtractTags` (143), `ExtractProperties` (193), `RenderMarkdown` (244), `RenderHTML` (255), `GenerateSnippet` (264), `ValidateContent` (349), `ExtractAll` (356), `RenameTag` (425).
  - Internally, `service` wraps `goldmark.Markdown` (yuin/goldmark) for parsing/HTML rendering, and delegates markdown-text re-rendering to a separate concrete helper type `renderer.MarkdownRenderer` (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go:15`, constructed via `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()` at line 20; used internally at `markdown.go:250` and `markdown.go:451`). Note: `MarkdownRenderer` is a plain concrete struct, not itself an interface implementation — it's an implementation detail of `service`, not a second implementation of `Service`.
  - Only one implementation of `Service` exists in the repo (confirmed via `grep -rln "func (s \*service)"` → only `markdown.go`).

### 3. Construction / instantiation sites (`markdown.NewService(...)`, defined at `markdown.go:85`)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` — inside `NewAPIV1Service(...)` (line 47): `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())`, stored into `MarkdownService` field at line 56. This is the main production wiring point.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44` — test helper construction.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54` — `markdown.NewService()` passed directly into `NewRSSService(...)`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427` — `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension())`.
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` — multiple unit-test constructions (lines 11, 16, 53, 156, 296, 310, 344, 353, 499/501, 512, 615, 644).

Note: `memopayload.NewRunner` (`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`) accepts a `markdown.Service` but I found **no call site** for `memopayload.NewRunner` anywhere in the repo (production or test) — it appears to be dead/unwired code, or intended for a CLI/maintenance entrypoint not present in the current tree.

### 4. Holders that depend on the interface type (field typed as `markdown.Service`, not the concrete `*service`)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35` — `APIV1Service.MarkdownService markdown.Service` (struct field). Set at construction line 56; consumed at:
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` — `s.MarkdownService` passed into `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload`.
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` — `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll(...)`.
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` — `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(...)`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` — `RSSService.MarkdownService markdown.Service` field; constructor `NewRSSService(profile, store, markdownService markdown.Service)` at line 58, field set line 62; consumed at line 339 (`s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML(...)`). Constructed at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`, passing `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` through (so the same instance is shared/injected across `APIV1Service` and `RSSService` — this is the DI pattern in use, i.e. manual constructor injection, no DI framework).
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14-16` — `Runner.MarkdownService markdown.Service` field; constructor `NewRunner(store, markdownService markdown.Service)` (line 19) and the package-level function `RebuildMemoPayload(_, memo, markdownService markdown.Service)` (line 74) both accept the interface type, not the concrete `service`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44-52` and `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427-432` — test structs/helpers that also hold/pass `markdown.Service` typed values.

### Summary of the dependency graph
```
markdown.Service (interface, markdown.go:31)
   └── implemented by: *service (markdown.go:58), created via markdown.NewService (markdown.go:85)

Construction: markdown.NewService() called in NewAPIV1Service (v1.go:47-56)
   → stored in APIV1Service.MarkdownService (interface-typed field)
   → same instance passed into rss.NewRSSService(...) at server.go:85
        → stored in RSSService.MarkdownService (interface-typed field)
   → passed into memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(...) at memo_service.go:108,447
   → memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService (interface-typed field) — constructed by NewRunner, but NewRunner has no found call site (unused/dead wiring)
```
